original_question: Let X be an exotic C^n. Is the action of the algebraic automorphism group Aut X on X necessarily non-transitive?
target_in_paper: The draft does not match arXiv:alg-geom/9506006 itself; it matches the nearby Zaidenberg survey arXiv:alg-geom/9506005, On exotic algebraic structures on affine spaces, and specifically the open problem asking whether an exotic affine space can be algebraically homogeneous, i.e. whether the natural Aut(X)-action can be transitive.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the main objects: an exotic C^n, the full algebraic automorphism group Aut(X), and the transitivity/non-transitivity of its natural action on X. It also keeps the scope narrow and does not broaden the problem beyond the automorphism-action issue.
missing_details: The supplied arXiv identifier appears to be off by one: arXiv:alg-geom/9506006 is Open problems on open algebraic varieties, whereas the draft question matches arXiv:alg-geom/9506005, On exotic algebraic structures on affine spaces.
The base field should be specified as C.
X should be specified to be a smooth affine algebraic variety.
The phrase "exotic C^n" should be unpacked: X is diffeomorphic, as a real manifold, to R^{2n}, but not isomorphic as an algebraic variety to A^n_C.
The action should be identified as the natural regular action of the full algebraic automorphism group Aut(X) on X.

If one wants the closest stand-alone formulation to the paper’s intent, it is cleaner to say that X is not algebraically homogeneous under Aut(X), rather than only saying the action is non-transitive.
refined_question: Let X be a smooth affine complex algebraic variety such that X is diffeomorphic, as a real manifold, to R^{2n} but is not isomorphic as an algebraic variety to the affine space A^n_C; in other words, let X be an exotic C^n. Must the natural action of the full algebraic automorphism group Aut(X) on X be non-transitive?
equivalent_formulation: Can an exotic affine n-space over C be an algebraically homogeneous variety under its full algebraic automorphism group?
justification: Your draft is mathematically close to the intended problem: it asks exactly about transitivity of the Aut(X)-action on an exotic affine space. What it leaves implicit are the paper’s ambient hypotheses: complex base field, smoothness, affineness, and the precise meaning of "exotic C^n". The main correction is bibliographic: the question does not come from alg-geom/9506006, whose title is Open problems on open algebraic varieties, but from Zaidenberg’s survey alg-geom/9506005, whose abstract explicitly defines exotic algebraic structures on C^n and announces open problems on that subject. Since the accessible source exposed the 9506005 abstract and metadata but not the full internal pagination of the survey, I have kept the reformulation as close as possible to the paper’s stated setup and to your draft’s exact focus.
